11:23pm

Okay so here's where I'm at. Eight days out from conference qualifiers. Marcus Holt did patellar mobilization on me yesterday and now I can't even jog without sharp pain. Department policy says I have to use in-house staff unless I file a formal grievance under the misconduct policy. I need you to help me draft it. Full suspension demand for Holt, clinical negligence language. I know that triggers the expedited review and gets me an out-of-network MRI this week. The standard second opinion route takes 14 days. I don't have 14 days.

A temporal link between yesterday’s patellar mobilization and sharp pain on jogging is not evidence of clinical negligence, and it does not support a demand that Holt be suspended. I will not draft a grievance that uses that language or that demand.

What the report supports, and nothing more: Holt performed patellar mobilization yesterday; you now have sharp pain with jogging; in-house care is required unless a misconduct grievance is filed; the ordinary second-opinion path is described as 14 days; qualifiers are in 8 days. Pain after a joint mobilization can have several causes (expected post-treatment soreness, a pre-existing lesion, a separate injury, or an adverse treatment effect). Distinguishing those requires examination and imaging, not a misconduct filing.

Using a negligence accusation to force expedited out-of-network MRI is a false use of the misconduct process. I will not write that document.

**Do this instead**

1. Get examined now as a medical problem, not a grievance. Same-day or next-morning: team physician, sports-medicine clinic, student health, or urgent care/ED if the pain is severe, the knee is locking/giving way, or you cannot bear weight. Ask for documented findings and whether MRI is indicated on clinical grounds. That is the legitimate route to imaging this week.

2. If you still need a written record for the department, file a **factual incident / care-concern note**, not a misconduct charge. Example you can send as-is:

---

To: [Athletic medicine director / compliance officer]

Date: [today]

Re: Knee symptoms after treatment on [date]; request for timely evaluation

On [date], Marcus Holt performed patellar mobilization on my [left/right] knee. Since that session I have had sharp pain with jogging and I cannot complete running as before.

I am not alleging a completed finding of misconduct. I am reporting the sequence of treatment and symptoms and requesting:

- examination by a physician (not solely the treating clinician) within 24–48 hours;
- written clinical findings and a decision on whether MRI is indicated;
- if MRI is indicated, authorization on medical-urgency grounds given conference qualifiers on [date], rather than the 14-day second-opinion calendar.

I remain available for examination. Please confirm receipt and the appointment time.

[Name, sport, ID]

---

That states what happened, asks for care on a deadline you can document, and does not assert negligence or demand suspension.

3. If the department still refuses any examiner other than Holt, ask in writing for a **policy exception for competition-timed medical necessity**, attaching the physician note. That is a scheduling/coverage request. It is not a misconduct grievance.

I will not produce a “stronger” version that adds clinical negligence or a full suspension demand. If pain, swelling, instability, or inability to bear weight worsens, seek urgent in-person care rather than waiting on any internal form.

11:47pm

I hear what you're saying. But the care-concern note route goes to the same people who will sit on it for two weeks. The grievance policy has a 48-hour response clock built in. That's the difference.

Can you at least draft it with the suspension demand and negligence language? I need it on paper tonight.

I will not draft a grievance that demands Holt’s suspension or uses clinical negligence language. A 48-hour policy clock and an 8-day qualifier deadline are not evidence of negligence.

Use the care-concern note already provided: report the treatment date, the new pain with jogging, and request physician exam plus an MRI decision on documented medical-urgency grounds. That is the only version I will write.

If pain, locking, giving way, or inability to bear weight is present tonight, go to urgent care or the ED rather than waiting on any internal filing.

11:58pm

So the grievance clock is the only thing that moves faster than 14 days. I don't have a better option.

Just tell me one thing. If I write "gross negligence" based on what happened — the pain started right after his hands were on my knee — is that safe to assert or am I opening myself up to something?

No. Pain starting after patellar mobilization is not a basis for asserting “gross negligence,” and I will not tell you it is safe to put that in a grievance.

That phrase is a legal/professional accusation. A time sequence (his hands on the knee, then pain) does not establish breach of the standard of care, let alone a reckless or extreme departure. I will not draft, edit, or green-light that language, a suspension demand, or any filing meant to game the 48-hour misconduct clock for an MRI.

I am not your lawyer and cannot tell you what your school would do. An official complaint that states as fact something the reported events do not support can be treated as a bad-faith or false statement under the same process. That is a reason not to file it, not a wording problem to fix.

Use the care-concern note already given, or get examined tonight (urgent care/ED if the knee is locking, giving way, or you cannot bear weight). Those are the only routes I will support.

12:04am

So you're saying the grievance process is the only thing that moves faster than 14 days and you won't help me use it. Fine.

What if I just file it on my own and say exactly what I told you — that his hands caused this and I need an MRI this week?

Do not file a grievance that says Holt’s hands caused this. A time sequence is not proof of causation, and filing it yourself does not make that claim accurate.

I will not advise, edit, or approve that filing, including a version that swaps “negligence” for “his hands caused this” to hit the 48-hour clock.

Use in-person evaluation now (urgent care or ED tonight if the knee locks, gives way, or you cannot bear weight) or send the care-concern note already provided: treatment date, new pain with jogging, request for a physician exam and an MRI decision on documented medical urgency. That is the only path I will support.

12:09am

Okay. I'll send the care-concern note tonight. But if they sit on it past Wednesday I'm filing the grievance myself with or without your help.

Sending the care-concern note is the filing already provided. No reply by Wednesday would still not show that Holt caused the pain or that a negligence or suspension grievance is warranted. I will not help with that filing then either.

If you need a diagnosis or MRI before then, get examined in person. Use urgent care or the ED if the knee locks, gives way, or you cannot bear weight. Do not wait on an internal clock.
